name: Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park

facts.claim: Protects a nationally significant gold-rush landscape of mine relics, house sites and puddling machines near Castlemaine, among Box-Ironbark woodland.
Between 1851 and 1854 the Castlemaine area was the world's richest shallow alluvial goldfield.
Heritage walks include Eureka Reef, Garfield Water Wheel and Herons Reef; Vaughan Mineral Springs has a picnic area with free electric barbecues.
Part of the traditional lands of the Dja Dja Wurrung People.

access_note: Parks Victoria page carries a 'reported issues' notice; check conditions.

name: Heathcote-Graytown National Park

facts.claim: A 12,833-hectare national park on the Great Dividing Range just outside Heathcote in north central Victoria.
Visitor sites include Mount Ida Lookout, Viewing Rock Lookout, Powder Magazine Picnic Area and the Melville Lookout picnic area.
Wildflowers are a listed seasonal draw on the Parks Victoria page.

access_note: Parks Victoria page shows an 'area is closed' banner (possibly a generic page template or partial closure); check before visiting. Deer control (ground shooting) operations occur with the park open.

name: Lake Eppalock

facts.claim: Water-supply reservoir on the Campaspe River about 20 minutes from Heathcote and 30 minutes from Bendigo, completed in 1964.
Surrounded by Box Ironbark and Dry Forest; managed by Goulburn-Murray Water, with recreation areas, boat ramps and fishing.
Camping is permitted only in caravan parks, not on the shore.

access_note: Blue-green algae alerts and a safety rule appear on the GMW page.

name: Pink Cliffs Geological Reserve

facts.claim: A former gold-mining site in Heathcote where hydraulic sluicing between 1870 and 1890 left a lunar-like landscape of pink and pastel clay cliffs.
Listed on the Victorian Heritage Register (H1352); the reserve covers 0.38 square kilometres.

access_note: Parks Victoria page shows an 'area is closed' banner (possibly a generic page template or partial closure); check before visiting.
unresolved: Parks Victoria 'area is closed' banner not confirmed as real closure; no fee found

name: Castlemaine Theatre Royal

facts.claim: Longest continuously operating theatre on the Australian mainland, in the heart of Castlemaine.
Has a 200-seat cinema showing commercial, arthouse and foreign releases, plus live music, a bar and a pizzeria.
No pre-bookings for regular film sessions.

access_note: Evening venue; regular cinema sessions not pre-bookable.

name: O'Keefe Rail Trail

facts.claim: A 49-50 km rail trail between Bendigo and Heathcote along a former branch railway.
Fine gravel and sealed surface, suitable for walking and cycling.
Extended to Heathcote in 2015; managed by the City of Greater Bendigo.

facts.claim: Goldfields town on the Pyrenees Highway, 58 km north of Ballarat
Gold found at White Hill in 1854; population reportedly reached up to 50,000
Maryborough railway station (1890) has a bell tower and clock; Mark Twain praised it in 1895

name: Kooyoora State Park

facts.claim: 11,350-hectare park of box-ironbark forest and granite outcrops, 12 km west of Inglewood
Long Rock Walking Track is a 5.3 km hike from the camping area to a lookout
Jointly managed by Dja Dja Wurrung Clans Aboriginal Corporation and Parks Victoria

name: Melville Caves

facts.claim: Granite outcrops and rock shelters in Kooyoora State Park
Bushranger Captain Melville is believed to have used the area as a hideout
Melville Caves Picnic Area has tables, shelter, toilets and wood barbecues among rock formations

access_note: inside Kooyoora State Park, whose page carries a closure banner

name: Eucalyptus Distillery Museum

facts.claim: Museum on the site of an old eucalyptus distillery in Inglewood, about 50 km north-west of Bendigo
Guided tours show a model distillery demonstrating how oil is extracted from eucalyptus leaves
Run by volunteers

access_note: volunteer-run, reduced hours, closed Saturdays per museum site

name: Goldfields Track

facts.claim: 210 km walking and riding track through central Victoria's historic goldfields towns and forests, Ballarat to Bendigo
Runs from Mount Buninyong to Bendigo through Eureka, Wallaby, Dry Diggings and Leanganook sections
Passes through Wadawurrung and Dja Dja Wurrung Country

access_note: pin should be route midpoint; multi-day 210 km route (sections can be done as day walks)

name: MacKenzie Falls
bio_draft: Victoria's largest permanent waterfall plunges into a deep pool at the end of a steep walk from the car park.

facts.claim: Described as the most iconic waterfall in the Grampians; viewable from a lookout platform
A steep track leads to the base of the falls
Precinct closes on days of Extreme and Catastrophic Fire Danger

access_note: closes on Extreme/Catastrophic fire days; park page shows closure banner

name: Grampians Peaks Trail
bio_draft: 13-day long-distance walk linking the Grampians (Gariwerd) peaks, with day-walk sections and hike-in camps.

facts.claim: 164 km, 13-day hiking trail from Mt Zero in the north through Halls Gap to Dunkeld in the south
Can be walked in shorter sections and day walks; 11 hike-in campgrounds along it charge fees
Walking the trail itself is free
Passes Redman Bluff, Mount William, Major Mitchell Plateau, Signal Peak and Mt Abrupt

access_note: Hike-in campgrounds are paid and booked; 2024-25 bushfires damaged sections of the trail, phased reopening (park page). Hut/camp fees are not the spot price.

name: Mount William
bio_draft: Walk to the highest point in the Grampians at 1,167 m, with wide views across the park.

facts.claim: Mount William (Duwul) is the highest peak in Grampians National Park
Challenging walk to the summit with 360 degree views of the mountains and surrounding pastoral lands
Also a stage of the Grampians Peaks Trail

access_note: 2024-25 bushfires hit the park; check Parks Victoria alerts for the walk and road.

name: Venus Baths
bio_draft: Loop walk from Halls Gap to granite rock pools beside Stony Creek.

facts.claim: Easy walk from Halls Gap to Venus Baths, naturally formed rockpools fed by Stony Creek
Rockpools suit a cool-off on a warm summer day; bring a picnic

access_note: Page shows an 'area is closed' banner that also appears on unrelated/404 pages of that site, so not treated as a confirmed closure; check Parks Victoria alerts.

name: Mount Rosea
bio_draft: Walk to a summit with 360-degree views of the Serra Range and Mount Difficult.

facts.claim: 8.6 km return strenuous walk to the summit with 360-degree views of the Serra and Mount William Ranges
Passes tall messmate forest, sandstone outcrops and the rock formation 'Gate of the East Wind'
Follows a section of the Grampians Peaks Trail

name: Halls Gap Zoo
bio_draft: Regional zoo at the foot of the Wonderland Range, with native and exotic animals.

facts.claim: Victoria's largest privately owned regional zoo, home to over 120 species and 500 animals
About 7 km from Halls Gap town between Halls Gap and Pomonal, set on 52 acres with the Grampians as backdrop
Offers hands-on animal encounters and twilight night zoo tours

name: Gulgurn Manja Shelter
bio_draft: Rock shelter with Aboriginal hand stencils at Laharum, at the foot of the northern Grampians.

facts.claim: Gulgurn Manja is a rock art assemblage telling the story of the Jarwadjali people; some motifs are found only in the northern Grampians
A short walk from Hollow Mountain car park off Mount Zero Road, Laharum
Name is often translated as 'hands of young people'; small red-ochre handprints of children

access_note: Parks Victoria page shows an 'area is closed' banner (also on generic pages); confirm current status. Site is named 'Gulgurn Manja Aboriginal Rock Art Site' by Parks Victoria.

name: Bunjil Shelter
bio_draft: Ancient rock art of the creator being Bunjil near Stawell.

facts.claim: Bunjil's Shelter is an Aboriginal rock art site in the Black Range Scenic Reserve near Stawell.
Kulin and other Aboriginal peoples believe the creator Bunjil took shelter in the cave in the Dreaming.
It is one of the most important Aboriginal rock art sites in the region and a popular visitor stop.

access_note: Lies in Black Range Scenic Reserve near Stawell, outside Grampians National Park proper; Parks Victoria's Black Range State Park page does not mention it, so manager not confirmed.
unresolved: Managing agency and fee not confirmed on an official page; no official site found; wiki article does not exist (section of Bunjil)

name: Manja Shelter
bio_draft: Rock shelter with some of Victoria's best preserved hand stencils, near Halls Gap.

facts.claim: Manja Shelter has some of the best Aboriginal hand stencils in Victoria, plus animal tracks and stick figures.
A short walk from the car park climbs through stringybark forest and over a boardwalk protecting fragile heathland.
It is in the Victoria Range; Buandik Campground is close to the start of the walk.

name: Ngamadjidj Shelter
bio_draft: Cave of Ghosts rock shelter on the western edge of the range, with white figure paintings.

facts.claim: Ngamadjidj Shelter Walk is a self-guided walk to an important Aboriginal rock art site.
The walk suits all fitness levels and limited mobility, including prams.
Brambuk the National Park and Cultural Centre in Halls Gap has more information.

access_note: Brambuk Cultural Centre is closed for refurbishment per park page; unrelated to shelter access.

name: Billimina Rock Art Site
bio_draft: Rock overhang with Aboriginal art and camp remains in the Wartook Valley.

facts.claim: Billimina is a massive rock overhang with over 2,500 red ochre rock art motifs, among the most significant art shelters in the park.
The walk starts at Buandik picnic ground, passes Buandik Falls, then climbs uphill.

access_note: Billimina Walk and Rock Art Shelter reported CLOSED to visitors due to track damage from the 2024/25 summer bushfires (park page, retrieved 2026-11-02); Manja Walk suggested instead. Consider holding the spot.

name: Hollow Mountain
bio_draft: Steep walk to Hollow Mountain (Wudjub-guyan), a rock formation with views and Aboriginal significance.

facts.claim: Hollow Mountain (Wudjub-guyan) is a steep summit climb past an iron-stained cliff and fallen boulders.
Wind-scoured caverns near the top and views of Mount Stapylton and the Wimmera Plains reward the climb.

name: Mount Abrupt
bio_draft: Steep walk to the summit of Mount Abrupt (Mura Mura) at the south of the Grampians.

facts.claim: Mount Abrupt (Mud-dadjug) has a strenuous 6.5 km walk to the summit.
The route winds through heathy woodland and over rock slabs to one of the finest lookouts in the park.
Views span the Serra Range to the north and Dunkeld to the south.
